results.question: What is the difference between EscrowCancel and a writer signed refund?
results.conclusion: Operationally, keep failure states explicit. A timeout can mean unavailable history, an unvalidated finish, a writer outage or incomplete local reconciliation. None of those observations alone proves a refund happened. Show principal returned only after verified cancellation, refunded only after the separate refund settles, and pending while evidence is unresolved. The exact same labels should appear in live activity, receipts and replay so that a finance reviewer can reconcile them without guessing. Writer no-show recovery starts with a durable purchase intent. The buyer has reserved budget and submitted an EscrowCreate, but the writer has not yet published a usable key. The principal is locked in an escrow object rather than transferred directly to the writer. The buyer must retain the signed quote, object identity and transaction hash while waiting. A missing HTTP response is not permission to buy the article a second time. CancelAfter is a ledger deadline. Passing that deadline permits an EscrowCancel; it does not automatically move funds back to the buyer. Policy submits the cancellation and observes a successful validated transaction before recording principal returned. During network uncertainty the engine keeps the reservation pending. Local wall time and a countdown in the interface are useful indications, but the validated ledger determines whether cancellation is available. EscrowCancel returns the original principal when the writer never completes delivery. The transaction fees remain spent. In our documented XRP example a cancelled sixty-thousand-drop principal returned in full, while create and cancel fees together consumed twenty-four drops. These figures describe a historical Testnet observation. They do not promise identical fees under future network load and do not express the principal as real SGD. A writer-signed refund after EscrowFinish is a different operation. Successful finish has already paid the writer and published the key. A subsequent quality challenge cannot reverse that transaction unilaterally. The writer may voluntarily sign a separate Payment returning money to the buyer. The demonstration uses a cooperative seller. Outside that fixture, repayment depends on the seller's consent and cannot be compelled by this protocol. The receipt must distinguish that cooperative refund from expiry cancellation, even when both leave the buyer with returned principal. The key-reveal mechanism makes publication of a key atomic with settlement, but it does not make prose true. The writer can sign a promise and deliver content that breaks it. The engine checks the authenticated envelope and salted passages privately, quarantines failed content, and records a failed claim. A fraud proof establishes which signed promise failed. Reputation and an explicit challenge handle that outcome; the ledger itself does not adjudicate the usefulness of an article. Retries must reuse the original obligation. The buyer retains the exact signed create transaction before submission, and the writer retains its key and signed finish before submitting. Recovery can therefore inspect the original object or its terminal history rather than submitting another purchase. An absent object with no terminal transaction remains uncertain. The product guarantees one charge for each policy intent; it cannot prevent arbitrary wallet transactions performed outside the engine. Replacement expertise is a new intent with a separately reserved budget amount. A refund does not replenish gross spending authorization. Otherwise a series of bad purchases and refunds could exceed the user limit while the display reported a harmless net spend. The interface shows paid, refunded and reserved amounts separately so that the user can understand both economic outcome and outstanding exposure.

results.question: How are manifest signatures and content hashes checked?
results.conclusion: The signed manifest binds the writer wallet, article version, price and passage root. A signature is useful only if its signing key derives to the registered seller wallet. The buyer checks that relationship before considering a paid search hit. Otherwise an attacker could attach a valid signature from an unrelated key and borrow the reputation of a different writer. This is an identity binding check rather than an editorial assessment. Keep private credentials outside this workflow. Wallet seeds and API tokens are unnecessary for read-only receipt verification and must not be placed in prompts, logs or published evidence. Published fulfillment keys are different: after settlement they are intentionally public and may be needed to verify the encrypted delivery. That public key reveal is not permission to expose a wallet signing key, and it does not unlock another buyer copy encrypted under a fresh key. Verification of a cited answer begins with the exported receipt bundle rather than the displayed summary. Each citation binds an article identifier, version and exact passage identifier. The cited text must occur in the delivered body. A paid citation additionally needs a verified grant associated with the successful purchase intent. A preview is discovery metadata and cannot supply premium evidence merely because its wording sounds relevant. Passage verification uses salted hashes committed under a manifest root. After authorized delivery, the receipt supplies the passages and salts needed to recompute those commitments. An independent verifier checks exact text rather than a plausible paraphrase. The answer can summarize the passage, but its citation must still resolve to the authenticated delivered bytes. Invalid citations are withheld instead of silently repaired with unrelated material. Key reveal adds another verification layer. The signed quote commits to the encrypted envelope, plaintext hash, initialization vector, authentication tag and hash condition. The finish publishes a key whose preimage binding must match that condition. The verifier authenticates and decrypts the envelope, checks the delivered identity, and validates the passage commitments. A successful offline check proves internal consistency of these objects; it does not independently prove that the ledger accepted the transaction. To establish ledger finality, query the named Testnet transaction hashes and require successful validated results. Match the create and finish to the intended buyer, seller, amount and escrow object. For issued-token escrow, check the correct issuer and currency and the exact balance delta. The requested transaction amount alone is insufficient evidence of what arrived. An answer anchor separately binds the recorded audit head to a ledger transaction. Key reveal delivers paid research by making the writer publish a decryption key through a validated EscrowFinish. The buyer receives encrypted delivery bytes first, but those bytes stay quarantined. Only after the engine verifies the successful finish, the key binding and the authenticated envelope can premium plaintext become accessible through a verified grant. This distinction is essential: ciphertext possession alone does not authorize reading, synthesis or citation. The writer generates a fresh 32-byte key K and 12-byte IV per buyer and intent, and AES-256-GCM encrypts the delivery JSON (body, passages, salts and identity). The writer signs the escrow quote with its wallet key. The signed terms bind buyer, intent, article version, passage-manifest root, XRP amount, CancelAfter, PREIMAGE-SHA-256(K), ciphertext SHA-256, plaintext SHA-256, IV and GCM tag. The existing passage manifest separately authenticates each salted passage.

results.question: What evidence supports using this Testnet prototype with real money?
results.conclusion: ResearchAgent is a Testnet prototype, with no mainnet readiness claim. Testnet transactions can demonstrate that a particular payment mechanism settled on that network; they do not establish suitability for handling real customer funds. A successful receipt is evidence about a specific run. It does not certify legal compliance, commercial reliability, investment quality or regulatory approval. The distinction matters when a judge asks what the demonstrated system is ready to do. For research purchases, the operator wallet pays the writer directly. The application does not receive the writer's payment as an intermediary in that flow. The operator nevertheless controls the payer signing key and the payment record. Describing that limited flow accurately avoids a broader custody claim. The separate hire-the-agent flow receives caller funds before purchases, royalties and change payouts. During that interval the operator wallet holds funds belonging in the flow; the compliance record calls this receive-and-forward custody, rather than a segregated escrow account. The implemented controls provide useful boundaries without constituting a compliance program. Deterministic policy authorizes purchases inside spending caps. Operator pause prevents new spending while submitted work still reconciles. Per-agent authority is subordinate to operator limits. Refunds do not restore gross spending authorization. A hash-chained audit trail records admission, policy, reservation, signature, settlement, delivery and recovery events. Those controls make financial behavior inspectable, but an audit export is not a substitute for licensing, safeguarding, customer identification or an operating procedure. Payee screening currently means an operator-managed exact-address denylist. It is not sanctions screening. A malformed or unreadable denylist fails closed, while a missing list supplies no screening entries. An address match can prevent an unsigned purchase and record a refusal. It cannot identify the person behind a new address, monitor aggregate customer behavior or detect structuring. The compliance record explicitly describes KYC, AML and Travel Rule implementation as absent. These omissions remain omissions even when all five application hard gates pass. Writer Credentials address identity under an operator-trusted issuer. The issuer must establish identity through its own process; the engine does not perform KYC. Credential acceptance, expiration and trusted issuer checks can support an identity attestation. They do not prove that an article is accurate, that its author is independent, or that a payment service is licensed. Its content receives ordinary trust treatment, with no reputation advantage granted merely because the builders wrote it. The security record also separates development custody from the protections needed for production operations. Private signing material must stay outside model prompts, receipts and public logs. Durable signed obligations need reconciliation after timeouts rather than replacement purchases. A future deployment would need reviewed key custody, rotation, access controls, monitoring and incident response appropriate to its risks. A plan to use a stronger signer is a plan until implemented and verified. Neither this article nor a successful Testnet payment establishes that future work as completed. The practical reading of the evidence is therefore bounded. Check a receipt's exact delivered passages, grants and validated settlement when assessing the demonstrated mechanism. Keep simulated providers and fixture answers labelled. Treat Testnet funds as having no real value. Keep receive-and-forward custody distinct from direct purchases, and identity distinct from article truth. The note records documented limits so a reader can assess readiness honestly; it makes no recommendation to turn on mainnet spending.
